title: C2999 — Steering wheel switch RH upper
introduction:
This reference maps the right-hand upper steering-wheel switch connector from its identity record through the cavity functions to its pigtail parts entry. I start with the component name before following the drawing: a familiar-looking plug is a lousy substitute for its name tag. Here, the illumination paths, control channel and right-hand switch return are the useful distinctions in the assignment table.

Match each pictured cavity label to the Cavity column, then read across that row. Asterisks leave circuit identifiers, colors and gauges unspecified; retain those gaps rather than supplying guesses. The parts table provides a catalog cross-reference. Physical access, viewing direction, probing, test limits and replacement instructions are outside this guide's scope, and its catalog codes and gauge convention are not defined.

edits.why: The printed drawing places the labeled circles in a vertical stack, with a broad rectangular feature to their left and projecting housing features to their right. These are landmarks for navigating the picture. They do not establish the physical viewing side, a release movement or an access route.

The function rows distinguish illumination from the switch's control-channel and right-hand return paths. Reading across a single cavity row preserves that association. An illumination ground label does not make every return path interchangeable, and a control-channel label alone supplies no expected voltage or resistance. Asterisks and unavailable terminal entries remain unspecified details.

The Kit List entry provides the route from connector identity to the pigtail record. Engineering Shell relates that record to the housing, while Service Part identifies the listed service item and Image names its illustration file. This is enough to trace the catalog relationship; it does not resolve the cavity table's unspecified wiring or teach pigtail installation.
